market_sizing.target_buyer: Founder / head brewer / production manager. In AU 1-10 person craft beverage companies the founder is almost always the buyer; in 20+ headcount producers the production manager or COO signs.
market_sizing.business_count_au: Estimated 40-80 active hard kombucha / low-no-alc craft beverage producers in AU. Independent kombucha scene has thinned post-Coke-Mojo and Lion-Remedy consolidation, but a long tail of <$2M revenue producers persists alongside no/low-alc startups (Lyre's, Naked Life, Heaps Normal adjacent). No published producer census; estimate derived from IBA + Independent Brewers Association overlap + SmartCompany 'independents not dead yet' coverage. [uncertain]
market_sizing.business_count_secondary: US: 200-400 hard kombucha brands per Brewers Association adjacent data and Bucha30 customer base. UK: 30-50 (Jarr, LA Brewery, Real Kombucha). NZ: 15-25 (Daily Organics, Good Buzz). CA: 30-60 (RISE, Tonica). All [uncertain] — no single authoritative census exists.
market_sizing.typical_size: 1-15 employees, AU$200K-$3M annual revenue. Founder-led with 1-3 production staff and 1-2 sales/marketing.
market_sizing.annual_revenue_band_aud: Most common band: AU$500K-$2M. Pre-revenue/sub-$250K tail exists but unlikely to buy MRP.
market_sizing.growth_trend: AU kombucha overall ~15% CAGR through 2033 (per outline). Hard kombucha specifically forecast at 18.6% CAGR globally (Grand View Research). No/low-alc RTD growing 10-15% CAGR to 2028 (IWSR / Drinks Trade). 31% of AU consumers now buy no-alcohol products.

fit_and_timing.addressable_window: Partially now; fully after excise-reporting capability is built. Lot tracking ships pre-launch which covers the FSANZ-side compliance, but ATO excise reporting for hard kombucha (>1.15% ABV) is a gap.
fit_and_timing.roadmap_dependency: Excise-duty calculation / ATO reporting export is a hard gap for hard-kombucha producers. Tank/fermenter management (not a stock-location concept) is a soft gap. Xero integration is highly desired (AU brewing accountants run on Xero).
fit_and_timing.typical_tier: Growth ($249) for early-stage producers; Pro ($499) once they hit retail distribution and multi-channel reconciliation.
fit_and_timing.regulatory_burden: 4 — FSANZ food-safety + ATO excise on alcoholic variants + AQIS for export + state-by-state liquor licensing. Heavier than non-alc beverages and most food categories.
fit_and_timing.time_to_value_days: 14-21 days. First useful output = batch-level COGS + lot-traceable inventory; longer than cosmetics because brewers expect tank/fermenter abstractions Manuva does not natively model.

economics.incumbent_pricing: Ekos ~US$300-600/mo (most common in AU craft beverage). Beer30 ~US$250-500/mo. Breww (UK, AU-aware) ~£150-400/mo. Bucha30 kombucha-specific ~US$300-500/mo. Crafted ERP $1K+/mo (enterprise). Spreadsheets + Xero is still the default sub-$1M segment.
economics.willingness_to_pay_aud: AU$200-450/mo range realistic. WTP is anchored by Ekos which is the category default and lands ~AU$450-900/mo. Manuva Growth ($249) is a clean undercut; Pro ($499) competes head-on but loses on excise/tank features. [uncertain]
economics.estimated_arpu_aud: AU$280/mo blended (mostly Growth with some Pro upgrades after retail-distribution unlock).
economics.expansion_revenue_potential: 3 — Tier upgrade as producers add retail and export channels. Lot tracking is table-stakes here so cannot be an upsell. Capacity planning and multi-location bonded-warehouse support could drive Pro upgrades. Excise add-on (if built) would be a clear paid module.
economics.churn_risk: 3 — Hard-kombucha specifically has consolidation churn (acquisition by big beverage) and category-fatigue churn (producers pivot to other RTDs or fold). Mid-life producers (year 2-4) are most stable. Founder burnout is meaningful.
economics.cac_estimate_aud: Cash CAC AU$80-150 (founder-led + community); founder-time CAC ~6-10 hours per closed deal (discovery + onboarding hand-holding for batch concepts) at notional $150/hr = AU$900-1500. Blended effective CAC AU$1000-1600.
economics.ltv_cac_ratio: ~3.2:1 if founder-time is fully loaded; ~30:1 on cash-only CAC. Healthy.
economics.typical_seat_count: 2-5 users (founder + head brewer + bookkeeper + warehouse). Strong wedge vs per-seat tools (Katana, MRPeasy) at 4+ seats.
economics.multi_channel_count: 3 — D2C web + wholesale to bottle-shops / cafes + on-premise (taprooms, events). Some also retail (Dan Murphy's, Coles Liquor for the bigger names).
economics.wholesale_b2b_mix: 60-80% wholesale, 20-40% D2C for established brands; inverse for early-stage. Wholesale invoicing and pricing tiers are a must-have.

outreach_fit.cold_outbound_feasibility: 3 — Brand websites and IBA member listings expose founder names and contact emails. LinkedIn is well-populated. Cold email is tolerated if specific (mention their tap list, last release). Cold-calling unwelcome. [uncertain]
outreach_fit.inbound_content_fit: 4 — 'Excise duty calculator for hard kombucha producers', 'Batch traceability for FSANZ audits', 'Ekos vs Manuva for sub-$2M kombucha brewers' are all clean SEO targets. Brews News and 'Booch News may accept guest articles.
outreach_fit.founder_market_fit_proxy: 3 — Brewers value technical credibility (recipe / yield / efficiency conversation) more than industry insider status. Solo founder can build credibility quickly by spending 2-3 weeks shadowing a producer. Lower trust bar than supplements or co-packing.
outreach_fit.case_study_acquisition_cost: Moderate — first 5 reference customers likely require 3-6 month design-partner motion + on-site visits. Founders are time-poor but proud of their craft so will give logo permission readily.

foot_in_door_fit.trial_to_paid_benchmark: Estimated 15-25% for CC-required trial in this segment given complexity of switching from Ekos / spreadsheets. Paid pilot ($249/mo × 3 mo, credited) likely 35-50%. [uncertain] — no segment-specific benchmark available.
foot_in_door_fit.recommended_foot_in_door_motion: Design partner (free 6mo + roadmap input on excise reporting + tank/fermenter abstraction) for the first 2-3 logos, then transition to paid pilot ($249/mo, 3 months, credited on conversion) once excise module ships. Founder-led outbound to IBA members + 'Booch News mentions. Co-marketing with Xero ProAdvisors who specialize in brewery accounting (small but identifiable cohort).
foot_in_door_fit.rollout_phase: Phase 2 (months 3-6, after lot tracking is battle-tested and Xero integration is live). Hard-kombucha specifically gated on excise module — Phase 3 unless that ships sooner.

competitive_context.current_dominant_tool: Ekos is the dominant craft-beverage ERP in AU breweries (probably 25-40% of >$1M producers). Spreadsheets + Xero is the default for <$1M producers (40-60%). Breww is gaining UK/AU share with its AU-specific excise module. Beer30, Bucha30, Crafted ERP, and BrewPlanner all have presence. Katana and Unleashed pick up cross-vertical share where founders came from another industry. [uncertain] on exact share splits.
competitive_context.switching_pain: 4 — Recipe / batch history migration is painful; ATO excise records must be preserved; integration with point-of-sale (taproom) and Xero must not break. Multi-month migration window typical.
competitive_context.competitor_gaps_for_this_segment: Ekos: USD-billed, expensive at AU$ FX (~AU$600/mo), no native Xero AU integration, weak on multi-channel D2C ecommerce. Bucha30: kombucha-specific but small vendor, US-centric, no AU excise. Spreadsheets: no lot traceability, no FSANZ audit trail. Katana: per-seat, no excise, weak on batch concepts. Manuva gaps to close before competing seriously: excise duty reporting, tank/fermenter modelling, taproom POS integration.
competitive_context.user_satisfaction_signals: Ekos G2/Capterra: complaints about price increases, slow support, US-centric features. Reddit r/kombucha and r/craftbeer: recurring threads on 'cheapest brewery software' and 'spreadsheet alternatives'. Brews News forum: periodic vendor comparison threads. [uncertain] on direct quotes — would require dedicated forum scrape.
competitive_context.competitor_concentration: Fragmented — no single tool >35%. Ekos leads but Breww, Bucha30, Beer30, Crafted ERP, Katana, and spreadsheets all hold meaningful share.
competitive_context.integration_dependency_list: Xero (critical AU), MYOB (some), POS for taprooms (Square, Lightspeed, Vend), Shopify (D2C), Untappd / Brews News brewery profile, ATO excise XML export, Faire (some wholesale), Australia Post / Sendle / Shippit, EFTPOS distributor invoicing.

profitability_math.realistic_12mo_customer_count_solo: 3-6 paying customers in 12 months. Excise gap + niche size + onboarding complexity caps faster acquisition. Most likely path: 2 design partners (months 3-6), 2-4 paid pilots converting (months 6-12).
profitability_math.path_to_first_3k_5k_mrr_aud: This segment alone will NOT hit AU$3-5K MRR in 12 months. It contributes 15-30% of the target. Path: (1) close 2 design partners via direct outreach at BrewCon + IBA member list, free 6 months in exchange for excise-feature input and logo; (2) ship excise-reporting MVP in months 4-6; (3) convert design partners to Growth tier; (4) inbound from 'Ekos alternative AU' SEO + Brews News article; (5) 4 customers × AU$249 = AU$1,000 MRR by month 12. Pair with the higher-volume segments (indie cosmetics, candle, coffee) to reach the AU$3-5K target.
profitability_math.customers_needed_for_1m_arr_aud: ~300 customers at AU$280/mo blended ARPU. Achievable only if hard-kombucha is bundled with the broader craft-beverage (cider, RTD, non-alc) category and excise tooling becomes a competitive moat.
profitability_math.solo_founder_bandwidth_fit: 2 — Onboarding requires understanding of batch / tank / excise workflows. Each design-partner deployment likely 30-50 hours of founder time. Support load high until excise module is automated.
profitability_math.break_even_contribution_months: 5-7 months at AU$249 Growth + 75% GM (cash CAC only); 12-18 months if founder-time is loaded.
profitability_math.gross_margin_sensitivity: Material erosion — excise compliance support is question-heavy, batch concepts confuse onboarding, and brewers expect responsive support during stocktake / month-end. Effective GM 65-75% rather than 80%+.
profitability_math.priority_ranking: 3 — Solid economics and high case-study appeal, but excise gap + niche size + heavy onboarding push it behind indie cosmetics (01), candle/soap (04), and coffee roasters (05) in the GTM sequence. Worth 1-2 design-partner slots for visual brand and to validate adjacency into broader craft beverage.
profitability_math.risks_and_notes: Risks: (1) Excise-reporting gap means hard-kombucha producers cannot self-serve onto Manuva today — must be roadmapped or de-prioritised. (2) Ekos is entrenched in producers >$2M revenue and will be hard to displace; sweet spot is sub-$1M brewers still on spreadsheets. (3) Coca-Cola / Lion / Bega consolidation has thinned the AU independent pool to a small number of high-quality logos. (4) Hard-kombucha specifically is a fashion-cycle category — non-alc and low-alc adjacent (Heaps Normal, Lyre's-style) is a safer bet long-term. Verify before going hard: actual AU IBA brewery member count by revenue band; whether Breww's AU excise module is now sufficient (would close the gap directly); whether one design partner can co-fund excise module via paid pilot.
